scope: The active 11 labels only; removed PEP, Crime-Organized Crime, and Crime-Theft & Property Crime. Retained-label definitions and reference values are unchanged.
prompt_policy: Compact English paraphrases of the reviewed definitions; not fitted or selected using evaluation examples.
shared_instruction: Classify only facts reported in the article. Specific attributed allegations and historical events count.

labels.label: Terrorism / Terrorist Financing
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of a specific terrorism-related activity, status or relationship supported in the article or attributed to an identifiable source. This broad label combines the four original subtopics.
Coverage: Terrorist acts, plots, planning or participation; providing, collecting, transferring or using money/assets for terrorists, organizations or acts; reported terrorist-organization characterization or specific membership/affiliation; and nonfinancial operational, material, logistical, training, recruitment, service, safe-house or travel-facilitation support. Preserve activity, financing, membership/affiliation or support as subtopic attributes; one does not imply all.
Boundary: Generic violence, war, political criticism, ordinary transfers, charitable activity, acquaintance/meetings, shared ethnicity/religion and rhetorical use of “terrorist” are insufficient. The terrorism link and actor/group role must be reported. Funding does not itself establish membership. Record allegation, charge, source characterization and judicial outcome separately; the label is not independent proof of crime.
labels.inclusion: Specific attributed terrorist act/plot; funds/assets with a reported terrorism purpose; supported terrorist group status or membership/affiliation; or concrete nonfinancial support with a reported terrorism link. At least one subtopic is sufficient. Every assigned label requires an exact supporting article span with article ID, actor/role and source attribution.
labels.exclusion: Generic violence/war, ordinary transfers/charity, political rhetoric, sympathy alone, meetings/contact, shared ethnicity/religion, or services without a supported terrorism link.
labels.question: Does the article report terrorism, terrorist financing, terrorist-group membership or operational support for terrorists, with an explicitly reported terrorism link?

labels.label: Regulatory
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of a specific regulatory matter/event involving an identified person, entity or activity, including formal regulator inquiry, alleged breach, established violation and formal enforcement/supervisory action. The original violation/action subtopics are combined; investigation is captured within the same broad scope.
Coverage: AML/CFT, reporting, licensing, prudential, market-conduct or consumer-protection issues; case-specific formal warnings, fines/penalties, license suspension/revocation, activity restrictions and debarment/procurement restrictions imposed by a competent authority. This includes debarment or cross-debarment by a multilateral development bank (e.g. World Bank, ADB, AfDB) and government procurement blacklisting. Preserve authority, target, issue, action and stage.
Boundary: Inquiry/suspicion is not a finding. A fine or no-admission settlement without a finding need not establish a proven breach. General guidance, education, broad market warnings, policy changes, ordinary licensing and industry surveys without a specific matter are insufficient. Classify multi-mandate agencies by their reported regulatory/criminal capacity; police action and court penalties receive other labels only for supported events.
labels.inclusion: Specific formal regulatory inquiry; a concrete alleged regulatory breach involving an identifiable subject/requirement; an authority finding; or an actual target-specific supervisory/enforcement measure. Record which is reported; one does not establish the others. Every assigned label requires an exact supporting article span with article ID, actor/role and source attribution.
labels.exclusion: General guidance, public education, policy announcements, routine license renewal, broad industry surveys or routine examinations without a specific reported matter. Police action and court punishment do not automatically become regulatory events.
labels.question: Does the article report a specific regulator investigation, regulatory breach, formal warning, license action, fine or development-bank/procurement debarment against an identified target?
labels.decision_concept: a specific regulatory matter or action

labels.label: Law Enforcement
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of official law-enforcement status, investigation or action in a specific criminal case/activity. The original alert/wanted, investigation and action subtopics share this broad label.
Coverage: Official criminal wanted/fugitive declarations and case-specific enforcement notices concerning suspects/cases; criminal investigations by police, prosecutors or criminal-capacity authorities; arrest, issue/execution of arrest/search warrants, searches, seizure of property/evidence and other reported formal criminal actions. Preserve investigated matter, action target and each actor’s role.
Boundary: Witnesses, victims and enforcement officials are not automatically suspects. Missing-person notices, witness requests treated as wanted status, journalistic/corporate inquiries, general police education, routine checks, civil-only seizure and sanctions blocking are excluded. Investigation is not proof and a warrant is not a conviction. A regulator receives this label only when acting in a reported criminal capacity; supervisory action is Regulatory.
labels.inclusion: Official criminal wanted/fugitive notice; formal criminal investigation into an identifiable subject/activity; or concrete formal criminal action such as an issued warrant, arrest, search or seizure. Preserve reported subtype and target. Every assigned label requires an exact supporting article span with article ID, actor/role and source attribution.
labels.exclusion: Missing-person notices; witness requests misread as wanted status; journalist/corporate inquiry; general policing/education; civil-only seizures; sanctions blocking; regulatory action without reported criminal capacity.
labels.question: Does the article report an official criminal investigation, wanted notice, arrest, criminal search warrant, search, seizure or another case-specific law-enforcement action?

labels.label: Judicial / Court
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of a specific judicial proceeding, event or disposition in a criminal case or civil, commercial, contractual or financial dispute. This combines the four original criminal-proceedings, criminal-judgment, sentencing and civil/commercial-proceedings subtopics.
Coverage: Formal prosecution/charges in a criminal judicial context, indictment, arraignment, hearings, trial and judicial pleas; guilty verdict/conviction and not-guilty verdict/acquittal; prison, criminal fines, probation or suspended sentences; appeal, vacatur, dismissal, termination or other specified dispositions; and filed civil/commercial lawsuits, hearings or judgments on contracts, ownership or financial claims. Record party role, case type, stage, charge and precise outcome separately.
Boundary: This label alone establishes neither guilt nor adversity; acquittal reporting qualifies too. Dismissal, bail release and withdrawal do not automatically mean acquittal. Police inquiry, threatened suit, private negotiation and purely regulatory punishment without a judicial event are insufficient. Separate historical events from current outcome when a case history is reported.
labels.inclusion: Actually reported criminal prosecution/court-process event, guilty verdict/conviction, acquittal, imposed criminal sentence, specified other formal disposition, or filed civil/commercial litigation/hearing/judgment. One supported subtopic is sufficient. Every assigned label requires an exact supporting article span with article ID, actor/role and source attribution.
labels.exclusion: Police inquiry alone; threatened/unfiled suit; private negotiations; regulatory penalty without a court event; hypothetical outcomes. Arbitration alone remains outside current scope pending VV policy.
labels.question: Does the article report an actual criminal or civil court proceeding, formal judicial charges, hearing, judgment, acquittal, sentence, appeal or filed lawsuit?
labels.decision_concept: a specific court proceeding or judgment

labels.label: Crime-Corruption
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of conduct or a specific allegation involving abuse of public power or entrusted authority for an improper personal or organizational benefit.
Coverage: Giving/receiving bribes, graft, kickbacks or improper payments, abuse of office, influence peddling and diversion of contracts/resources for private benefit. Embezzlement/misappropriation may also qualify when entrusted-authority abuse is reported. Mentioning an official or PEP alone is insufficient.
Boundary and overlap: A specific attributed allegation or supported conduct description is sufficient for reporting classification, not independent proof. Political criticism, inefficiency, an unexplained gift or rhetorical use of “corrupt” is insufficient. Reported appropriation may also receive Crime-Theft & Property Crime; independently supported financial deception may receive Crime-Fraud. Several labels for one event do not establish several independent offenses.
labels.inclusion: An identified event with bribery, kickbacks or entrusted-power abuse is reported or attributed to a source. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Political criticism, inefficiency, an unexplained gift, or the word “corrupt” used rhetorically.
labels.question: Does the article report bribery, graft, kickbacks or abuse of public power or entrusted authority for improper personal or organizational benefit?

labels.label: Crime-Fraud
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of a deceptive scheme, intentional misrepresentation or fraudulent conduct intended to obtain economic benefit or cause financial loss. This is not an umbrella for every financial offense.
Coverage: Investment scams, Ponzi/fictitious investment schemes, money obtained through false promises, estafa/swindling, loan/payment/insurance/invoice fraud, fabricated financial claims and deceptive identity misuse. Tax fraud, securities fraud and online scams are covered where deception is reported.
Boundary and overlap: Business failure, investment loss, accounting error, debt or contract breach alone is not fraud. Money laundering, bribery and other financial offenses do not automatically receive Crime-Fraud without deception evidence. Tax fraud may receive Crime-Tax Crime plus Crime-Fraud; securities fraud Crime-Securities & Market Crime plus Crime-Fraud; deceptive phishing Crime-Cybercrime plus Crime-Fraud.
labels.inclusion: Specific financial deception or an attributed fraud allegation/charge in an identified event. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Money laundering, bribery, tax evasion or market manipulation without reported deception. Mistake, poor investment return, or a generic financial-crime reference.
labels.question: Does the article report an intentional deceptive scheme or misrepresentation to obtain economic benefit or cause financial loss, rather than merely debt or business failure?

labels.label: Crime-Forgery & Counterfeiting
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of unlawful creation, alteration, reproduction or knowing use of forged documents, currency, identities, securities, instruments or counterfeit items, or a specific forgery/counterfeiting allegation.
Coverage: Deliberate falsification of documents/certificates, fake identification, counterfeit currency, forged securities/financial instruments, forged signatures and criminal presentation/use of these items. Possession is covered only where knowledge or the relevant offense is reported.
Boundary and overlap: Administrative errors, authorized copies, marked props/replicas, generic “fake news” and unknowing possession are insufficient. Forgery for financial gain may also receive Crime-Fraud; forged tax records in a tax offense Crime-Tax Crime; and criminal digital identity forgery Crime-Cybercrime. Preserve item type and maker/user role.
labels.inclusion: An attributed forgery/counterfeiting offense or specific intentional falsification/knowing use. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Accidental errors, authorized copies, harmless props, generic “fake news”, or unknowing possession alone.
labels.question: Does the article report unlawful creation, alteration or knowing use of forged documents, signatures, IDs, currency or counterfeit products?

labels.label: Crime-Cybercrime
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of a crime or specific allegation targeting computers, networks, systems or digital data, or involving a material digital mechanism.
Coverage: Unauthorized intrusion/access, criminal hacking, malware, ransomware, unlawful data theft/alteration, intentional system attacks, phishing, digital identity theft and digitally enabled fraud/extortion. A breach qualifies when linked to a reported attack, unauthorized access or offense. Record attacker, suspect, victim and affected-organization roles separately.
Boundary and overlap: System failure, accidental exposure, a vulnerability without reported crime, routine internet use or a suspect sending ordinary email is insufficient. A breached entity is not thereby a perpetrator. Digital deception may also receive Crime-Fraud; property/data appropriation may overlap only where the other label’s criteria are met.
labels.inclusion: An intentional unauthorized act or attributed cyber offense. For cyber-enabled conduct, describe how digital systems materially enabled it. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Accidental data leak, system outage, routine online business, a suspect simply using email, or a victim blamed merely for being breached.
labels.question: Does the article report hacking, malware, criminal data theft, phishing, digital identity theft or another crime with a material digital mechanism?

labels.label: Crime-Trafficking & Smuggling
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of illicit trafficking, trade or movement of people, substances, weapons, goods or controlled items, or human trafficking for exploitation.
Coverage: Drug/controlled-substance trafficking; human trafficking including sexual exploitation or forced labor; migrant smuggling; illicit arms/prohibited-equipment trafficking; goods smuggling and unlawful shipments; and illicit trade/movement of protected wildlife or natural resources. Human trafficking need not cross a border. Preserve subtype, commodity and person/entity role only as supported by the text.
Boundary and overlap: Lawful migration, authorized trade/transport, a shipment without illicit context and web-traffic usage are insufficient. Wildlife trafficking may also receive Crime-Environmental & Wildlife Crime; reported abduction/violence may receive Crime-Violent Crime. Arms trafficking alone does not establish an arms embargo.
labels.inclusion: Specific attributed trafficking or smuggling activity. Human trafficking does not require crossing a border. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Lawful migration, ordinary shipping, transport of legal commodities, trafficking used to mean web traffic.
labels.question: Does the article report illicit drug trade, human trafficking for exploitation, migrant smuggling, arms trafficking, goods smuggling or illegal wildlife/resource trade?

labels.label: Crime-Violent Crime
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of an offense or specific allegation involving physical violence or threats of physical harm against people/property, or kidnapping/hostage-taking.
Coverage: Murder/attempted murder, violent assault, abduction, kidnapping for ransom, hostage-taking, violent robbery and extortion involving physical violence or threats of physical injury. Record victim, suspect and reported-perpetrator roles separately.
Boundary and overlap: Accidents, accidental injury, verbal disputes, economic threats or information blackmail without physical threats, and metaphorical “attacks” are insufficient. Do not force nonviolent extortion into this label; preserve offense wording for scope review. Violent robbery may also receive Crime-Theft & Property Crime. Violence alone does not establish terrorism, genocide, war crimes or crimes against humanity.
labels.inclusion: A reported violent offense, abduction or explicit threat of physical harm involving an identified event. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Generic conflict, metaphorical attack, nonviolent blackmail, or accidental injury without alleged crime.
labels.question: Does the article report physical violence, threats of physical injury, murder, assault, kidnapping, hostage-taking or violent robbery, rather than only economic threats?
labels.decision_concept: violent crime or physical harm threats

labels.label: Crime-Environmental & Wildlife Crime
labels.english_definition:
Definition: Reporting of a crime or specific allegation involving unlawful exploitation, destruction, hunting, trade or movement of environmental resources or wildlife.
Coverage: Illegal logging, illegal fishing/mining, protected-species hunting, wildlife trafficking/illegal trade, unlawful resource/habitat destruction and other specifically reported environmental offenses. Illegal pollution/discharge is covered when specific criminal or unlawful conduct is reported.
Boundary and overlap: General ESG criticism, emissions without illegality allegations, accidents alone, authorized activity and technical noncriminal breaches alone are insufficient. Wildlife trafficking may also receive Crime-Trafficking & Smuggling; regulator inquiry/action may receive Regulatory. A species or mine name alone does not establish crime. Where illegality depends on an external reference, record its source and date.
labels.inclusion: Specific criminal/unlawful environmental or wildlife conduct, including an attributed allegation. Save the exact supporting text span(s), entity/role, source attribution and event/case ID.
labels.exclusion: Lawful resource use, accidental pollution without reported wrongdoing, generic sustainability criticism, or a technical noncriminal breach alone.
labels.question: Does the article report illegal logging, fishing, mining, protected-wildlife exploitation or trade, unlawful habitat destruction or criminal pollution?
